moses.name: Moses
moses.role: Prophet who leads Israel from Egypt
moses.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
moses.importance: Moses does not act in Judges. Caleb gets Hebron as Moses had said. The Kenites are the family of his brother-in-law. Judges 18:30 calls the priest Jonathan his grandson in this text.
moses.connections: Son of Amram and Jochebed. Brother of Aaron and Miriam. Husband of Zipporah.

aaron.name: Aaron
aaron.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
aaron.importance: Aaron does not act in Judges. Judges 20:28 names him as the grandfather of Phinehas the priest.
aaron.connections: Son of Amram and Jochebed. Father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

joshua.name: Joshua
joshua.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
joshua.importance: The book opens after his death. Chapter 2 tells again how he sent the people home and died. The people served the LORD while he and his elders lived. The people born after them did not know the LORD.
joshua.connections: Son of Nun. He led Israel in the book of Joshua.

eleazar.name: Eleazar
eleazar.role: Priest, son of Aaron and father of Phinehas
eleazar.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
eleazar.importance: Eleazar does not act in Judges. Judges 20:28 names him as the father of Phinehas the priest.
eleazar.connections: Son of Aaron. Father of Phinehas.

caleb.name: Caleb
caleb.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
caleb.importance: He offers his daughter Achsah to the man who takes Kiriath Sepher. Othniel takes it and marries her. Caleb gives Achsah the upper and lower springs. He receives Hebron and drives out the three sons of Anak.
caleb.connections: Son of Jephunneh. Father of Achsah. Othniel is his relative and becomes his son-in-law.

balak.name: Balak
balak.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
balak.importance: Balak does not act in Judges. Jephthah names him in his message to the king of Ammon. He asks whether Balak ever fought against Israel.

phinehas.name: Phinehas
phinehas.role: Priest who stands before the ark
phinehas.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
phinehas.importance: He stands before the ark when Israel asks the LORD about Benjamin. Israel asks whether to go out to battle a third time. The LORD says to go up and promises victory the next day.
phinehas.connections: Son of Eleazar. Grandson of Aaron.

sihon.name: Sihon
sihon.role: King of the Amorites at Heshbon
sihon.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
sihon.importance: Sihon does not act in Judges. Jephthah tells how Israel asked to pass through his land. Sihon did not trust Israel and fought at Jahaz. Israel won and took the Amorite land.
sihon.connections: Jephthah names him in his message to the king of Ammon.

joseph.name: Joseph
joseph.role: Ancestor recalled through a tribal name
joseph.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
joseph.importance: Joseph himself does not appear. The house of Joseph attacks Bethel in chapter 1. A man shows them the way in, and they let his family go. They later force the Amorites to work.
joseph.connections: Son of Jacob and Rachel. Husband of Asenath. Father of Ephraim and Manasseh.

judah.name: Judah
judah.role: Ancestor recalled through a tribal name
judah.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
judah.importance: Judah himself does not appear. His tribe goes first against the Canaanites, with Simeon’s help. In chapter 15 its men tie up Samson for the Philistines. In chapter 20 the LORD sends Judah first against Benjamin.
judah.connections: Son of Jacob and Leah. Father of Perez and Zerah through Tamar.

reuben.name: Reuben
reuben.role: Ancestor recalled through a tribal name
reuben.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
reuben.importance: Reuben himself does not appear. Deborah’s song asks why his people sat among the sheepfolds. It says they searched their hearts by their streams.
reuben.connections: Son of Jacob and Leah. Brother of Joseph.

simeon.name: Simeon
simeon.role: Ancestor recalled through a tribal name
simeon.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
simeon.importance: Simeon himself does not appear. His tribe goes with Judah to fight the Canaanites. The two tribes then destroy Zephath, and the city is called Hormah.

levi.name: Levi
levi.role: Ancestor recalled through a tribal name
levi.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
levi.importance: Judges never names Levi himself. Two Levites appear near the end of the book. One becomes priest for Micah and then for Dan. The other travels with the woman from Bethlehem.

benjamin.name: Benjamin
benjamin.role: Ancestor recalled through a tribal name
benjamin.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
benjamin.importance: Benjamin himself does not appear. His tribe does not drive the Jebusites out of Jerusalem. Ehud comes from this tribe. It later shields the men of Gibeah and is nearly wiped out in war.
benjamin.connections: Son of Rachel. Full brother of Joseph.

ephraim.name: Ephraim
ephraim.role: Ancestor recalled through a tribal name
ephraim.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
ephraim.importance: Ephraim himself does not appear. His tribe holds the Jordan for Gideon and kills Oreb and Zeeb. Its men scold Gideon, and he calms them. They threaten Jephthah, and Gilead’s men kill 42,000 of them.
ephraim.connections: Son of Joseph and Asenath. Brother of Manasseh.

manasseh.name: Manasseh
manasseh.role: Ancestor recalled through a tribal name
manasseh.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
manasseh.importance: Manasseh himself does not appear. His tribe leaves Canaanites in Beth Shean, Megiddo, and other towns. Gideon comes from a poor family in this tribe. Its men answer Gideon’s call against Midian.
manasseh.connections: Son of Joseph and Asenath. Brother of Ephraim.

zebulun.name: Zebulun
zebulun.role: Ancestor recalled through a tribal name
zebulun.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
zebulun.importance: Zebulun himself does not appear. His tribe sends men with Barak to Mount Tabor. Deborah’s song says they risked their lives. They also answer Gideon’s call, and the judge Elon comes from this tribe.
zebulun.connections: Son of Jacob and Leah. His name also identifies a later tribe.

issachar.name: Issachar
issachar.role: Ancestor recalled through a tribal name
issachar.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
issachar.importance: Issachar himself does not appear. Deborah’s song says his princes were with Deborah and Barak. The judge Tola is a man of Issachar.
issachar.connections: Son of Jacob and Leah. His name also identifies a later tribe.

dan.name: Dan
dan.role: Ancestor recalled through a tribal name
dan.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
dan.importance: Dan himself does not appear. The Amorites push his tribe into the hill country. Samson comes from a family of Dan. In chapter 18 six hundred men of Dan take Laish and name it Dan.
dan.connections: Son of Jacob and Bilhah. His name also identifies a later tribe.

naphtali.name: Naphtali
naphtali.role: Ancestor recalled through a tribal name
naphtali.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
naphtali.importance: Naphtali himself does not appear. Barak comes from Kedesh in Naphtali and calls its men to fight Sisera. Deborah’s song says they risked their lives. They also follow Gideon against Midian.
naphtali.connections: Son of Jacob and Bilhah. His name also identifies a later tribe.

gad.name: Gad
gad.role: Ancestor recalled through a tribal name
gad.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
gad.importance: Judges does not use Gad’s name. His tribe lived east of the Jordan. Deborah’s song says only that Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan.
gad.connections: Son of Jacob and Zilpah. His name also identifies a later tribe.

asher.name: Asher
asher.role: Ancestor recalled through a tribal name
asher.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
asher.importance: Asher himself does not appear. His tribe lives among the Canaanites it did not drive out. Deborah’s song says Asher sat still by the sea. Its men later join Gideon against Midian.
asher.connections: Son of Jacob and Zilpah. His name also identifies a later tribe.

othniel.name: Othniel
othniel.role: Caleb’s relative who takes Debir and judges Israel
othniel.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
othniel.importance: He takes Kiriath Sepher, also called Debir, and marries Achsah. Later the LORD’s Spirit comes on him, and he judges Israel. He defeats Cushan Rishathaim. The land rests forty years until he dies.
othniel.connections: Son of Kenaz. He marries Caleb’s daughter Achsah.

achsah.name: Achsah
achsah.role: Caleb’s daughter who asks for springs
achsah.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
achsah.importance: Caleb gives her as wife to Othniel. She gets Othniel to ask her father for a field. Then she asks Caleb for springs of water. He gives her the upper and lower springs.
achsah.connections: Daughter of Caleb and wife of Othniel.

adonibezek.name: Adoni-bezek
adonibezek.role: Ruler caught by Judah at Bezek
adonibezek.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
adonibezek.importance: Judah and Simeon fight him at Bezek, and he runs. They catch him and cut off his thumbs and big toes. He says he did the same to seventy kings. They bring him to Jerusalem, and he dies there.
adonibezek.connections: Enemy of Judah and Simeon. No family is named.

cushan-rishathaim.name: Cushan-rishathaim
cushan-rishathaim.role: King of Mesopotamia who rules Israel
cushan-rishathaim.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
cushan-rishathaim.importance: The LORD sells Israel into his hand, and Israel serves him eight years. Israel cries to the LORD. Othniel goes out to war and defeats him.
cushan-rishathaim.connections: Enemy of Othniel. No family is named.

ehud.name: Ehud
ehud.role: Left-handed man of Benjamin who kills Eglon
ehud.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
ehud.importance: He hides a short sword on his right thigh and brings Israel’s payment to Eglon. Alone with the king, he stabs him and locks the doors. He escapes and leads Israel to the Jordan crossings. They defeat Moab, and the land rests eighty years.
ehud.connections: Son of Gera. He carries tribute to Eglon.

eglon.name: Eglon
eglon.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
eglon.importance: He takes the city of palm trees and rules Israel eighteen years. Ehud brings him payment and says he has a secret message. Eglon sends his servants out, and Ehud kills him. This man is not the Canaanite town named Eglon.
eglon.connections: He gathers Ammon and Amalek to fight Israel.

shamgar.name: Shamgar
shamgar.role: Man who strikes 600 Philistines with an ox goad
shamgar.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
shamgar.importance: He strikes six hundred Philistines with an ox goad and saves Israel. Deborah’s song says the roads were empty in his days. The book says nothing more about him.

deborah.name: Deborah
deborah.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
deborah.importance: She lives under a palm tree between Ramah and Bethel and judges Israel. She gives Barak the LORD’s command and goes with him. She tells him the day to attack. Then she and Barak sing the song in chapter 5.
deborah.connections: Wife of Lappidoth. She calls Barak to lead the army.

barak.name: Barak
barak.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
barak.importance: He will not go to battle unless Deborah goes too. He leads ten thousand men down Mount Tabor and beats Sisera’s army. He chases Sisera and finds him dead in Jael’s tent. He sings the victory song with Deborah.
barak.connections: Son of Abinoam, from Kedesh in Naphtali.

sisera.name: Sisera
sisera.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
sisera.importance: He brings nine hundred iron chariots to the river Kishon. His army loses, and he runs on foot to Jael’s tent. She gives him milk, covers him, and kills him as he sleeps. In the song his mother waits at the window for him.
sisera.connections: Captain of the army of Jabin. Jael kills him.

jabin-judges.name: Jabin
jabin-judges.role: King of Canaan who reigns in Hazor
jabin-judges.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
jabin-judges.importance: He has nine hundred iron chariots and crushes Israel for twenty years. He does not appear in the battle himself. After Sisera dies, Israel grows stronger until it destroys him.
jabin-judges.connections: Sisera is captain of his army. Heber’s house is at peace with him.

jael.name: Jael
jael.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
jael.importance: She goes out to Sisera and invites him into her tent. She gives him milk and covers him. While he sleeps she drives a tent peg through his head. She shows Barak the body, and the song calls her blessed.

heber.name: Heber
heber.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
heber.importance: He leaves the other Kenites and sets his tent near Kedesh. His house is at peace with Jabin. So Sisera runs to his wife’s tent. Heber himself does nothing in these chapters.
heber.connections: Husband of Jael. His household has peace with Jabin.

gideon.name: Gideon
gideon.role: Judge who defeats Midian with 300 men
gideon.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
gideon.importance: The LORD’s angel sends him to save Israel from Midian. He pulls down Baal’s altar, asks for signs, and beats Midian with three hundred men. He punishes Succoth and Penuel and kills two kings. He refuses to rule, but his gold ephod becomes a trap for Israel.
gideon.connections: Son of Joash. Father of Jether, Jotham, and Abimelech. Also called Jerubbaal.

joash-gideon.name: Joash
joash-gideon.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
joash-gideon.importance: He owns an altar of Baal, and Gideon pulls it down. The men of the city want Gideon dead. Joash says Baal should fight for himself if he is a god. Gideon is later buried in Joash’s tomb.
joash-gideon.connections: Father of Gideon. An Abiezrite who owns the oak at Ophrah.

oreb.name: Oreb
oreb.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
oreb.importance: He flees after Gideon’s night attack. Ephraim’s men kill him at the place called Oreb’s rock. They bring his head to Gideon beyond the Jordan.
oreb.connections: Prince of Midian beside Zeeb. Ephraim’s men kill them both.

zeeb.name: Zeeb
zeeb.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
zeeb.importance: He flees after Gideon’s night attack. Ephraim’s men kill him at Zeeb’s wine press. They bring his head to Gideon. Gideon points to the two deaths to calm Ephraim’s anger.
zeeb.connections: Prince of Midian beside Oreb. Ephraim’s men kill them both.

zebah.name: Zebah
zebah.role: King of Midian chased by Gideon
zebah.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
zebah.importance: He and Zalmunna camp at Karkor with about fifteen thousand men. Gideon attacks, and they run, but he catches them. They admit they killed Gideon’s brothers at Tabor. Gideon kills them both.

zalmunna.name: Zalmunna
zalmunna.role: King of Midian chased by Gideon
zalmunna.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
zalmunna.importance: Gideon chases him and Zebah across the Jordan and catches them. Gideon learns they killed his brothers at Tabor. His son Jether will not kill them. The two kings tell Gideon to do it himself, and he does.

jether.name: Jether
jether.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
jether.importance: Gideon tells him to kill Zebah and Zalmunna. He does not draw his sword. He is afraid because he is still a youth. Gideon kills the kings himself.

abimelech-judges.name: Abimelech
abimelech-judges.role: Gideon’s son who becomes king at Shechem
abimelech-judges.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
abimelech-judges.importance: He hires men with Shechem’s silver and kills his brothers at Ophrah. Shechem makes him king, then turns on him after three years. He destroys Shechem, but a woman at Thebez drops a millstone on his head. He is not the Abimelech of Genesis.
abimelech-judges.connections: Son of Gideon and his concubine from Shechem. Half brother of Jotham.

jotham-gideon.name: Jotham
jotham-gideon.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
jotham-gideon.importance: He hides when Abimelech kills his brothers. From Mount Gerizim he tells Shechem about trees that pick a thorn bush as king. He warns of fire between Abimelech and Shechem, then flees to Beer. He is not the later king Jotham.
jotham-gideon.connections: Youngest son of Gideon. Half brother of Abimelech.

gaal.name: Gaal
gaal.role: Man who turns Shechem against Abimelech
gaal.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
gaal.importance: He moves to Shechem, and its men trust him. At a harvest feast he mocks Abimelech and dares him to fight. Abimelech’s men come in the morning and chase him to the gate. Zebul drives him and his brothers out of Shechem.
gaal.connections: Son of Ebed. He comes to Shechem with his brothers.

zebul.name: Zebul
zebul.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
zebul.importance: He hears Gaal’s boast and secretly warns Abimelech. He tells Abimelech to hide in the field at night. When Gaal sees men coming, Zebul says they are shadows. Then he dares Gaal to fight and later drives him out.
zebul.connections: Abimelech’s officer. He works against Gaal.

tola.name: Tola
tola.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
tola.importance: He rises to save Israel after Abimelech. He judges Israel twenty-three years. He lives in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim and is buried there.
tola.connections: Son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar.

jair.name: Jair
jair.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
jair.importance: He judges Israel twenty-two years. His thirty sons ride thirty donkeys and hold thirty towns in Gilead. The towns are called Havvoth Jair. He is buried in Kamon.
jair.connections: Father of thirty sons. No parent is named.

jephthah.name: Jephthah
jephthah.role: Gileadite leader called back from the land of Tob
jephthah.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
jephthah.importance: His brothers drive him out, and he lives in Tob. The elders of Gilead bring him back to fight Ammon. He vows to offer whatever comes out of his house, and his daughter comes out. He later fights Ephraim and judges Israel six years.
jephthah.connections: Son of Gilead and a woman described as a prostitute. Father of one daughter.

jephthah-daughter.name: Jephthah’s daughter
jephthah-daughter.role: Unnamed only child caught by her father’s vow
jephthah-daughter.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
jephthah-daughter.importance: She comes out to meet her father with tambourines and dances. She tells him to keep his vow. She asks for two months on the mountains with her friends. Her father then does as he vowed, and Israel’s daughters remember her each year.
jephthah-daughter.connections: Daughter of Jephthah. Her name is not given in Judges.

ibzan.name: Ibzan
ibzan.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
ibzan.importance: He judges Israel seven years. He sends his thirty daughters to marry outside his clan. He brings in thirty wives from outside for his sons. He is buried at Bethlehem.
ibzan.connections: Father of thirty sons and thirty daughters.

elon.name: Elon
elon.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
elon.importance: He judges Israel ten years. He dies and is buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun. The book says nothing more about him.
elon.connections: A man of Zebulun. No family is named.

abdon.name: Abdon
abdon.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
abdon.importance: He judges Israel eight years. He has forty sons and thirty grandsons who ride seventy donkeys. He is buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim.

samson.name: Samson
samson.role: Nazirite strongman who fights the Philistines
samson.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
samson.importance: He marries a Philistine woman, and a lost bet over a riddle starts a feud. He burns their grain and kills a thousand men with a jawbone. He tells Delilah his hair is the secret, and the Philistines blind him. At their feast he pulls down the house and dies with them.
samson.connections: Son of Manoah and his unnamed wife. He marries a woman of Timnah and later loves Delilah.

manoah.name: Manoah
manoah.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
manoah.importance: He prays for the man of God to come back and teach them. He asks the angel about the child and offers a young goat. When the angel rises in the flame, he fears they will die. He later goes to Timnah with Samson, who is buried in his tomb.
manoah.connections: A Danite from Zorah, husband of Samson’s unnamed mother.

samson-mother.name: Samson’s mother
samson-mother.role: Unnamed woman told she will bear Samson
samson-mother.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
samson-mother.importance: The LORD’s angel tells her she will bear a son. He tells her to drink no wine and never cut the boy’s hair. She tells Manoah both times the angel comes. When Manoah fears death, she says the LORD accepted their offering.
samson-mother.connections: Wife of Manoah and mother of Samson.

samson-wife.name: Samson’s wife at Timnah
samson-wife.role: Unnamed Philistine woman Samson marries at Timnah
samson-wife.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
samson-wife.importance: The wedding guests say they will burn her and her father’s house. She cries to Samson for seven days and gets the riddle’s answer. Her father gives her to another man. After Samson burns the fields, the Philistines burn her and her father.
samson-wife.connections: Samson’s first wife. Her father later gives her to another man.

delilah.name: Delilah
delilah.role: Woman who learns the secret of Samson’s strength
delilah.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
delilah.importance: The Philistine lords offer her silver to learn Samson’s secret. She asks him four times, and three times he lies. He tells her at last that his hair has never been cut. She has his head shaved as he sleeps, and the Philistines take him.
delilah.connections: Samson loves her. The Philistine lords pay her to trap him.

micah-judges.name: Micah
micah-judges.role: Man of Ephraim with a house of gods
micah-judges.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
micah-judges.importance: He returns silver he took from his mother, and she has an image made. He hires a young Levite as his priest. Men of Dan take his images and his priest, and he cannot stop them. He is not the prophet Micah.
micah-judges.connections: Son of an unnamed mother. He hires a young Levite as priest.

jonathan-priest.name: Jonathan
jonathan-priest.role: Levite priest for Micah, then for Dan
jonathan-priest.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
jonathan-priest.importance: A young Levite leaves Bethlehem and becomes Micah’s priest for pay. Men of Dan offer him a whole tribe, and he goes with Micah’s images. Judges 18:30 names Dan’s priest Jonathan, likely this same Levite. Old copies differ over whether his ancestor’s name is Moses or Manasseh.
jonathan-priest.connections: Judges 18:30 calls him son of Gershom, son of Moses.

levite-traveler.name: The Levite traveler
levite-traveler.role: Unnamed Levite whose report starts a war
levite-traveler.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
levite-traveler.importance: He goes to Bethlehem to bring the woman home. At Gibeah a mob surrounds the house, and he pushes her out to them. He cuts up her body and sends the pieces through Israel. At Mizpah he tells the tribes of the crime but leaves out his own act.
levite-traveler.connections: The text calls the woman from Bethlehem his concubine. He travels with a servant.

word.languageNote: This is the dictionary form of the name “Levite.”

levite-concubine.name: The woman from Bethlehem
levite-concubine.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
levite-concubine.importance: She leaves the Levite and goes to her father’s house for four months. He comes for her, and they stop at Gibeah for the night. The men of the city abuse her all night. She falls at the door, and the text gives her no words.
levite-concubine.connections: The text calls her the Levite’s concubine. Her father lives in Bethlehem.
